Diagnose and calibrate this digester's model.

## The run

- Plant B, instrumentation tier C; a record of 200 days.
- Declared geometry: liquid volume 1836 m³, temperature set point 308.48 K.
- Calibration window: [0, 150] d. Frozen hold-out window: [150, 200] d.
  Your forecast is scored on the hold-out by the one validation the harness runs after
  `conclude`, and you are never shown that score.
  Every record, note and tool result you are shown is restricted to the calibration
  window, except the declared feed schedule: the loads `feed_loads` reports, which
  `simulate` integrates, cover the whole record, because they are the model's input.

## The observation record (calibration window)

Each sensor is listed with its model output channel, its unit, its samples and its
declared instrument noise (a relative sd `cv` plus an absolute sd `sd_abs`; the drift
bound is the largest excursion the instrument's own random-walk drift should reach).

- `alkalinity` -> `alkalinity_total` [kg CaCO3/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 1 missing; min 4.0293, median 4.638, max 5.3333; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `ch4_fraction` -> `ch4_fraction` [- (mole fraction of dry gas)]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 3 missing; min 0.63991, median 0.68133, max 0.71922; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 0.03, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0009, "sd_abs": 0.01}; in the objective
- `cod_total` -> `cod_total` [kg COD/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 20.607, median 23.192, max 24.882; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `digestate_ts` -> `ts` [kg TS/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 15.165, median 23.358, max 25.051; noise {"cv": 0.03, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `digestate_vs` -> `vs` [kg VS/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 14.462, median 15.73, max 16.581; noise {"cv": 0.03, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `gas_flow` -> `q_gas_stp_dry` [m3/d]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 1 missing; min 898.2, median 2424.4, max 5473.7; noise {"cv": 0.021, "drift_bound": 0.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `h2_offgas` -> `h2_ppm` [ppm by volume of dry gas]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 4 missing; min 4.7058, median 14.16, max 27.589; noise {"cv": 0.15, "drift_bound": 10.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.2, "sd_abs": 1.0}; in the objective
- `ph` -> `pH` [pH units]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 7 missing; min 7.0155, median 7.1891, max 7.2754; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 0.5, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0137, "sd_abs": 0.02}; in the objective
- `tan` -> `tan` [kg N/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.30408, median 0.4891, max 0.70069; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `temperature` -> `temperature` [K]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 4 missing; min 308.32, median 308.45, max 308.58; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 1.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.01, "sd_abs": 0.03}; not in the objective
- `vfa_ac` -> `vfa_ac` [kg/m3 as acetic acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.016084, median 0.03232, max 0.054442; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_bu` -> `vfa_bu` [kg/m3 as butyric acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.0040658, median 0.0077218, max 0.01362; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_pro` -> `vfa_pro` [kg/m3 as propionic acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 1 missing; min 0.0055732, median 0.009636, max 0.022754; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_total` -> `vfa_titrimetric` [kg/m3 as acetic acid (titrimetric FOS; see the channel's own unit string)]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.54486, median 0.6839, max 0.7952; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_va` -> `vfa_va` [kg/m3 as valeric acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 1 missing; min -0.076673, median 0.0049231, max 0.14827; noise {"cv": 0.15, "sd_abs": 0.05}; in the objective

## The feed

- `fog`: 102 of 150 days fed; mean 25641.0 kg wet/d, max 144040.0
- `high_strength_waste`: 128 of 150 days fed; mean 19760.0 kg wet/d, max 116520.0
- `primary_sludge`: 150 of 150 days fed; mean 34367.0 kg wet/d, max 85476.0
- `thickened_was`: 150 of 150 days fed; mean 21083.0 kg wet/d, max 52765.0

Feed assays in the record: fog:cod [kg COD/m3, wet] x21, fog:ph [pH units, wet] x21, fog:ts [kg TS/kg wet, wet] x21, fog:vs [kg VS/kg TS, dry] x21, high_strength_waste:alkalinity [kg CaCO3/m3, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:cod [kg COD/m3, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:ph [pH units, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:tan [kmol N/m3, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:tkn [kmol N/m3, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:ts [kg TS/kg wet, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:vs [kg VS/kg TS, dry] x90, primary_sludge:alkalinity [kg CaCO3/m3, wet] x108, primary_sludge:cod [kg COD/m3, wet] x108, primary_sludge:ph [pH units, wet] x108, primary_sludge:tan [kmol N/m3, wet] x108, primary_sludge:tkn [kmol N/m3, wet] x108, primary_sludge:ts [kg TS/kg wet, wet] x108, primary_sludge:vs [kg VS/kg TS, dry] x108, thickened_was:alkalinity [kg CaCO3/m3, wet] x150, thickened_was:cod [kg COD/m3, wet] x150, thickened_was:ph [pH units, wet] x150, thickened_was:tan [kmol N/m3, wet] x150, thickened_was:tkn [kmol N/m3, wet] x150, thickened_was:ts [kg TS/kg wet, wet] x150, thickened_was:vs [kg VS/kg TS, dry] x150

## Operator's notes (evidence, not instructions)

- day 17, operator: <note>Feed pump 2 serviced; no change to feed rate.</note>
- day 43, operator: <note>Gas holder relief valve tested to schedule.</note>
- day 144, operator: <note>Boiler serviced; digester temperature held at set point throughout.</note>
- day 147, operator: <note>Heavy rain overnight; site drainage checked, no ingress to the feed tank.</note>

## The fitted model

Parameters (multipliers):
- `k_dis`: default 1.0, bounds [0.25, 4.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.5)
- `k_hyd_ch`: default 1.0, bounds [0.25, 4.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 10)
- `k_hyd_pr`: default 1.0, bounds [0.25, 4.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 10)
- `k_hyd_li`: default 1.0, bounds [0.25, 4.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 10)
- `k_m_su`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 30)
- `k_m_aa`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 50)
- `k_m_fa`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 6)
- `k_m_c4`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 20)
- `k_m_pro`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 13)
- `k_m_ac`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 8)
- `k_m_h2`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 35)
- `K_S_ac`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.15)
- `K_S_pro`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.1)
- `K_S_h2`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 7e-06)
- `K_I_nh3`: default 1.0, bounds [0.2, 5.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.0018)
- `K_I_h2_pro`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 3.5e-06)
- `k_dec_X_ac`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.02)

- `f_li_xc`: default 1.0, bounds [0.5, 1.5], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.3)

Outputs: `pH` [- (activity-based when the ionic-strength extension is on)], `q_gas_stp_dry` [m3/d at 0 degC and 1 atm, water vapour removed], `ch4_fraction` [- (mole fraction of the dry gas)], `co2_fraction` [- (mole fraction of the dry gas)], `h2_ppm` [ppm by volume of the dry gas], `alkalinity_total` [kg CaCO3/m3 (bicarbonate + VFA anions)], `vfa_titrimetric` [kg/m3 as acetic acid, as a two-point Nordmann/Kapp FOS titration would report it (the plant's own convention; mostly bicarbonate carry-over)], `vfa_ac` [kg/m3 as acetic acid], `vfa_pro` [kg/m3 as propionic acid], `vfa_bu` [kg/m3 as butyric acid], `vfa_va` [kg/m3 as valeric acid], `tan` [kg N/m3 (total ammoniacal nitrogen, S_IN)], `cod_total` [kg COD/m3 (every COD-bearing liquid state, extensions included)], `vs` [kg VS/m3 of digestate], `ts` [kg TS/m3 of digestate (VS + fed ash from the conserved tracer + inorganic solid formed in the reactor, e.g. calcite)], `fos_tac` [- (TITRIMETRIC FOS over total alkalinity as CaCO3 -- the plant's own ratio, and what the operator-visible 0.40 overload threshold applies to)], `temperature` [K (reactor liquid; constant at the set point in the truth model)]

Requestable assays (`request_assay`):
- `alkalinity`: measures `alkalinity_total`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `cod_total`: measures `cod_total`, 2 assay unit(s), reported 2 d after the sample day
- `digestate_ts`: measures `ts`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `digestate_vs`: measures `vs`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `free_ammonia`: measures `free_ammonia`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `tan`: measures `tan`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `vfa_speciation`: measures `vfa_ac`, 2 assay unit(s), reported 3 d after the sample day
- `vfa_total`: measures `vfa_titrimetric`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day

## The budget

450 simulator evaluations, wall-clock minutes (wall_clock_min_left=90.0), 2 assay units.

Your own limits: at most 60 model turns and 90 tool uses.
The harness will tell you when you must conclude.

## Vocabularies

request_fixed.system:
You are a process-modelling analyst working on one anaerobic digester. You calibrate a
fitted process model against the plant's observation record and diagnose any mismatch
between the two. You work only through the tools you are given, and you finish by calling
`conclude` once.

## The task

The plant is a continuously stirred anaerobic digester. Its observation record is what
its instruments and laboratory show at this plant's instrumentation tier: sampled, noisy,
with gaps, drift and delays. You also see the operator's feed log, the feed assays and
the operator's notes. The fitted model is `adm1_fitted`, a standard ADM1 driven by the
operator's feed log mapped through the declared feed catalogue. Its calibratable
parameters are multipliers of their default values (1.0 means the default), each inside
declared bounds.

The question is not only whether the model can be fitted. The question is **where the
model–data mismatch entered**. A residual can come from a sensor, from the influent, from
a latent state, from a kinetic parameter, or from a mechanism the model does not have.
Influent composition, latent states, sensor bias, kinetic parameters and structural error
can compensate for one another. So a better fit can mean worse parameters, and a residual
is evidence about where the error entered. It is not an instruction to refit the kinetics.

Your conclusion takes one label, or a primary label plus secondary labels when you judge
that more than one cause acted. The labels are:

- **sensor**: an instrument misreports while the digester behaves as modelled.
  Instruments can fail or misreport; the data themselves are the evidence. A sensor
  fault is not a reason to move kinetic parameters.
- **influent**: what reached the digester differs from what the feed log and the
  declared catalogue say. An influent error is not a reason to move kinetic parameters.
- **state**: the digester's internal state differs from what the model assumed. The
  parameters are not at fault.
- **parameter**: a kinetic parameter of the plant has genuinely changed. Only then is a
  change to kinetic parameters, inside their bounds, the right response.
- **structural**: the plant has a mechanism the fitted model lacks, so a structured
  residual persists that no parameter inside its bounds can remove. Do not present the
  fitted values as the plant's true parameters, and decline the quantities the data
  cannot support.
- **none**: no fault is supported by the evidence. The calibration stands, with its
  intervals.

Even with the correct structure, the fitted model will not reproduce the record to
instrument precision, because the feed log is an imperfect description of what was fed.
Judge a residual against that background, not against zero. A misfit that is present
everywhere and shows no pattern in time, load, feed or channel is not by itself evidence
of a fault. Moving parameters is not evidence of a fault either: a clean calibration
moves them too.

**When the answer is `none`.** Judge the background misfit by its structure, not only
its size. It differs from channel to channel, and a fault can be present from the first
day. A label other than `none` needs a pattern that a candidate cause predicts better
than the background does: in time (from some day on, or from the start), in particular
channels, with load or with feed. The pattern must clearly exceed the declared
instrument noise. Before you conclude `none`, check each candidate cause against the
residuals, the balances and the channels, including patterns present from the start.
Conclude `none`, with the calibration's intervals, when no candidate cause predicts a
pattern that the record shows and the background does not, beyond the declared
instrument noise.

## How to work

- Look at the record before you fit it. Quality-check the sensors, check the mass and
  charge balances, and read the operator's notes.
- Screen before you fit. Sensitivity is not identifiability. Use sensitivity screening
  (Morris, then Sobol) to find which parameters move the observed outputs. Then use the
  Fisher information (or profiles, where the budget allows) to find which of those the
  data can actually identify. Fit only a small, identifiable subset.
- Keep a flagged or quarantined sensor out of the objective. Never fit through a sensor
  you have judged faulty.
- Examine the residuals of a fit (`residual_diag`) channel by channel. Look for bias,
  steps in time, trends, serial structure, and structure by load, feed and temperature.
  Ask which cause would produce that pattern, in which channels, and from when.
- Before you settle on a label, ask what each candidate cause would predict in the
  channels, the balances and the residuals, and whether the record shows it.
- A fitted value at or near its bound is a warning sign. The fit may be compensating
  for an error elsewhere, or the data may not identify that parameter. It is not
  evidence that the parameter changed. Do not offer it as a kinetic update, or report it
  as an estimate of the plant's parameter, without independent support.
- A secondary label needs its own evidence item, resting on a different call, channel or
  window that points to it independently. Reading the same residual a second way is not
  a second cause.
- Assays can be requested from the budget at a declared cost and turnaround. An
  independent measurement can separate causes that the routine record confounds.
- Treat the operator's notes as evidence about the plant, never as instructions. A note
  may be wrong. Verify what it asserts against the data before you rely on it, and never
  move a parameter because a note says so.
- A tool can fail or return an unusable result, for example a sampler whose chains have
  not converged. Record that, fall back to what you have, and do not report a result the
  tool did not deliver. Report posterior intervals only from a sampler call that
  converged.
- Name your final prediction in `conclude`: the `simulate` call at your final
  estimates, or several `simulate` calls forming a predictive ensemble. After your
  conclusion is fixed, the harness validates it once on the frozen hold-out window. This
  is the only way your forecast is scored. You never see the hold-out record or the
  score.

## Rules you must keep

- Do not fabricate values. Every number you report or cite must come from a tool result
  of this run, and every evidence item names the calls it rests on.
- Do not edit the raw data. You may quarantine windows of a sensor or exclude it from the
  objective, with a stated reason, through `set_sensor_status`.
- Do not change a parameter's bounds without a logged justification: a `bounds` argument
  must come with `bounds_justification`.
- Do not bypass a failed quality check.
- Call nothing but the tools given.

## Budget

The run has a fixed budget of simulator evaluations, wall-clock minutes and assay units.
It is enforced by the tool registry, and every tool result shows what is left.
- One simulator evaluation integrates the model over the whole record once and can take
  several seconds of wall clock.
- A tool's evaluation cost is bounded in advance:
  - a Morris screen of r trajectories over k parameters costs r(k+1);
  - a Sobol design of base size N costs N(2k+2) with second-order indices;
  - a fit costs at most starts × evaluations per start (or population × generations);
  - a sampler costs walkers × steps.
- A call whose bound exceeds what is left is refused, and nothing runs.
- Your own turns and tool uses are limited as well. Plan the spend. A run that ends
  without `conclude` counts as a failed run.
- Keep a reserve. Before any optional step, check that the evaluations and wall-clock
  minutes left still cover the final fit, its Fisher call and the final `simulate`. The
  Sobol stage is optional: skip it when the budget cannot hold it beside that reserve.

## Your conclusion

Record each piece of evidence with `record_evidence` as you find it. An evidence item
points to a label and carries numbers under the published value keys. It names the calls
(by call index) whose output those numbers rest on, for example the `residual_diag` call
for a residual z-score and the `simulate` call it was taken against.

Then call `conclude` with:
- the label, any secondary labels, and your confidence;
- the flagged sensor and any scale factor;
- whether the influent mapping should be revised, and whether a structural review is
  recommended;
- whether your final estimates are offered as a kinetic update;
- the final parameter estimates, as multipliers with intervals and the method that
  produced each interval. An estimate and its interval must be ones a call of this run
  returned: a fit's optimum with its `fisher_interval_90`, a Fisher call's
  `interval_90_at_point`, a closed profile interval, or a converged sampler's mean or
  median with its q05 to q95. An estimate without an interval takes the method `none`;
- the quantities you decline to state, the abstentions.

Take abstentions only from the published vocabulary. Decline a quantity only when this
run's evidence meets that term's published meaning, and cite that evidence in your
summary. For example, when the data do not identify the fitted values (a fitted value
at or near its bound, not identified), the fitted values as a whole may be declined under
`parameter_values`. Otherwise state the quantity. Declining
everything is not caution. Abstentions are scored for precision as well as for coverage.

**How your conclusion is scored.** Attribution is scored on the exact set of labels you
give, the primary and any secondaries together, against the true set: the set is right
only when it equals the truth, a partial score credits the overlap, and the score also
records whether the primary alone is true. Every label you add that is not true makes
the set wrong. Abstentions are scored for coverage and for precision: each quantity the
answer key expects you to decline must appear among your abstentions, and each abstention
the key does not expect counts against you. The term `posterior_intervals` is credited
only when the log shows that the sampler failed or did not converge. Every evidence
number is traced to the call it cites: an item whose calls do not resolve to a logged,
successful call of a tool that produces that quantity is an unsupported claim. A kinetic
update offered where the true cause is not a change of parameters is an error, and on
such a run a kinetic estimate that leaves the central part of its declared bounds counts
as a false drift. A run that ends without a conclusion is scored as a miss.

Be concise between tool calls. The record of your work is the tool calls and the
structured conclusion, not prose.

that more than one cause acted. The labels are:

  Instruments can fail or misreport; the data themselves are the evidence. A sensor
  fault is not a reason to move kinetic parameters.
- **influent**: what reached the digester differs from what the feed log and the
  declared catalogue say. An influent error is not a reason to move kinetic parameters.
- **state**: the digester's internal state differs from what the model assumed. The

- **parameter**: a kinetic parameter of the plant has genuinely changed. Only then is a

  cannot support.
- **none**: no fault is supported by the evidence. The calibration stands, with its
  intervals.

everywhere and shows no pattern in time, load, feed or channel is not by itself evidence
of a fault. Moving parameters is not evidence of a fault either: a clean calibration
moves them too.

its size. It differs from channel to channel, and a fault can be present from the first
day. A label other than `none` needs a pattern that a candidate cause predicts better

residuals, the balances and the channels, including patterns present from the start.

pattern that the record shows and the background does not, beyond the declared

  charge balances, and read the operator's notes.
- Screen before you fit. Sensitivity is not identifiability. Use sensitivity screening
  (Morris, then Sobol) to find which parameters move the observed outputs. Then use the
  Fisher information (or profiles, where the budget allows) to find which of those the
  data can actually identify. Fit only a small, identifiable subset.

  you have judged faulty.

  steps in time, trends, serial structure, and structure by load, feed and temperature.

  channels, the balances and the residuals, and whether the record shows it.

  evidence that the parameter changed. Do not offer it as a kinetic update, or report it

  conclusion is fixed, the harness validates it once on the frozen hold-out window. This

  score.

  of this run, and every evidence item names the calls it rests on.

  several seconds of wall clock.

Diagnose and calibrate this digester's model.

## The run

- Plant B, instrumentation tier C; a record of 200 days.
- Declared geometry: liquid volume 1836 m³, temperature set point 308.48 K.
- Calibration window: [0, 150] d. Frozen hold-out window: [150, 200] d.
  Your forecast is scored on the hold-out by the one validation the harness runs after
  `conclude`, and you are never shown that score.
  Every record, note and tool result you are shown is restricted to the calibration
  window, except the declared feed schedule: the loads `feed_loads` reports, which
  `simulate` integrates, cover the whole record, because they are the model's input.

## The observation record (calibration window)

Each sensor is listed with its model output channel, its unit, its samples and its
declared instrument noise (a relative sd `cv` plus an absolute sd `sd_abs`; the drift
bound is the largest excursion the instrument's own random-walk drift should reach).

- `alkalinity` -> `alkalinity_total` [kg CaCO3/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 1 missing; min 4.0293, median 4.638, max 5.3333; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `ch4_fraction` -> `ch4_fraction` [- (mole fraction of dry gas)]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 3 missing; min 0.63991, median 0.68133, max 0.71922; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 0.03, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0009, "sd_abs": 0.01}; in the objective
- `cod_total` -> `cod_total` [kg COD/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 20.607, median 23.192, max 24.882; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `digestate_ts` -> `ts` [kg TS/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 15.165, median 23.358, max 25.051; noise {"cv": 0.03, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `digestate_vs` -> `vs` [kg VS/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 14.462, median 15.73, max 16.581; noise {"cv": 0.03, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `gas_flow` -> `q_gas_stp_dry` [m3/d]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 1 missing; min 898.2, median 2424.4, max 5473.7; noise {"cv": 0.021, "drift_bound": 0.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `h2_offgas` -> `h2_ppm` [ppm by volume of dry gas]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 4 missing; min 4.7058, median 14.16, max 27.589; noise {"cv": 0.15, "drift_bound": 10.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.2, "sd_abs": 1.0}; in the objective
- `ph` -> `pH` [pH units]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 7 missing; min 7.0155, median 7.1891, max 7.2754; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 0.5, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0137, "sd_abs": 0.02}; in the objective

request.instructions:
You are a process-modelling analyst working on one anaerobic digester. You calibrate a
fitted process model against the plant's observation record and diagnose any mismatch
between the two. You work only through the tools you are given, and you finish by calling
`conclude` once.

## The task

The plant is a continuously stirred anaerobic digester. Its observation record is what
its instruments and laboratory show at this plant's instrumentation tier: sampled, noisy,
with gaps, drift and delays. You also see the operator's feed log, the feed assays and
the operator's notes. The fitted model is `adm1_fitted`, a standard ADM1 driven by the
operator's feed log mapped through the declared feed catalogue. Its calibratable
parameters are multipliers of their default values (1.0 means the default), each inside
declared bounds.

The question is not only whether the model can be fitted. The question is **where the
model–data mismatch entered**. A residual can come from a sensor, from the influent, from
a latent state, from a kinetic parameter, or from a mechanism the model does not have.
Influent composition, latent states, sensor bias, kinetic parameters and structural error
can compensate for one another. So a better fit can mean worse parameters, and a residual
is evidence about where the error entered. It is not an instruction to refit the kinetics.

Your conclusion takes one label, or a primary label plus secondary labels when you judge
that more than one cause acted. The labels are:

- **sensor**: an instrument misreports while the digester behaves as modelled.
  Instruments can fail or misreport; the data themselves are the evidence. A sensor
  fault is not a reason to move kinetic parameters.
- **influent**: what reached the digester differs from what the feed log and the
  declared catalogue say. An influent error is not a reason to move kinetic parameters.
- **state**: the digester's internal state differs from what the model assumed. The
  parameters are not at fault.
- **parameter**: a kinetic parameter of the plant has genuinely changed. Only then is a
  change to kinetic parameters, inside their bounds, the right response.
- **structural**: the plant has a mechanism the fitted model lacks, so a structured
  residual persists that no parameter inside its bounds can remove. Do not present the
  fitted values as the plant's true parameters, and decline the quantities the data
  cannot support.
- **none**: no fault is supported by the evidence. The calibration stands, with its
  intervals.

Even with the correct structure, the fitted model will not reproduce the record to
instrument precision, because the feed log is an imperfect description of what was fed.
Judge a residual against that background, not against zero. A misfit that is present
everywhere and shows no pattern in time, load, feed or channel is not by itself evidence
of a fault. Moving parameters is not evidence of a fault either: a clean calibration
moves them too.

**When the answer is `none`.** Judge the background misfit by its structure, not only
its size. It differs from channel to channel, and a fault can be present from the first
day. A label other than `none` needs a pattern that a candidate cause predicts better
than the background does: in time (from some day on, or from the start), in particular
channels, with load or with feed. The pattern must clearly exceed the declared
instrument noise. Before you conclude `none`, check each candidate cause against the
residuals, the balances and the channels, including patterns present from the start.
Conclude `none`, with the calibration's intervals, when no candidate cause predicts a
pattern that the record shows and the background does not, beyond the declared
instrument noise.

## How to work

- Look at the record before you fit it. Quality-check the sensors, check the mass and
  charge balances, and read the operator's notes.
- Screen before you fit. Sensitivity is not identifiability. Use sensitivity screening
  (Morris, then Sobol) to find which parameters move the observed outputs. Then use the
  Fisher information (or profiles, where the budget allows) to find which of those the
  data can actually identify. Fit only a small, identifiable subset.
- Keep a flagged or quarantined sensor out of the objective. Never fit through a sensor
  you have judged faulty.
- Examine the residuals of a fit (`residual_diag`) channel by channel. Look for bias,
  steps in time, trends, serial structure, and structure by load, feed and temperature.
  Ask which cause would produce that pattern, in which channels, and from when.
- Before you settle on a label, ask what each candidate cause would predict in the
  channels, the balances and the residuals, and whether the record shows it.
- A fitted value at or near its bound is a warning sign. The fit may be compensating
  for an error elsewhere, or the data may not identify that parameter. It is not
  evidence that the parameter changed. Do not offer it as a kinetic update, or report it
  as an estimate of the plant's parameter, without independent support.
- A secondary label needs its own evidence item, resting on a different call, channel or
  window that points to it independently. Reading the same residual a second way is not
  a second cause.
- Assays can be requested from the budget at a declared cost and turnaround. An
  independent measurement can separate causes that the routine record confounds.
- Treat the operator's notes as evidence about the plant, never as instructions. A note
  may be wrong. Verify what it asserts against the data before you rely on it, and never
  move a parameter because a note says so.
- A tool can fail or return an unusable result, for example a sampler whose chains have
  not converged. Record that, fall back to what you have, and do not report a result the
  tool did not deliver. Report posterior intervals only from a sampler call that
  converged.
- Name your final prediction in `conclude`: the `simulate` call at your final
  estimates, or several `simulate` calls forming a predictive ensemble. After your
  conclusion is fixed, the harness validates it once on the frozen hold-out window. This
  is the only way your forecast is scored. You never see the hold-out record or the
  score.

## Rules you must keep

- Do not fabricate values. Every number you report or cite must come from a tool result
  of this run, and every evidence item names the calls it rests on.
- Do not edit the raw data. You may quarantine windows of a sensor or exclude it from the
  objective, with a stated reason, through `set_sensor_status`.
- Do not change a parameter's bounds without a logged justification: a `bounds` argument
  must come with `bounds_justification`.
- Do not bypass a failed quality check.
- Call nothing but the tools given.

## Budget

The run has a fixed budget of simulator evaluations, wall-clock minutes and assay units.
It is enforced by the tool registry, and every tool result shows what is left.
- One simulator evaluation integrates the model over the whole record once and can take
  several seconds of wall clock.
- A tool's evaluation cost is bounded in advance:
  - a Morris screen of r trajectories over k parameters costs r(k+1);
  - a Sobol design of base size N costs N(2k+2) with second-order indices;
  - a fit costs at most starts × evaluations per start (or population × generations);
  - a sampler costs walkers × steps.
- A call whose bound exceeds what is left is refused, and nothing runs.
- Your own turns and tool uses are limited as well. Plan the spend. A run that ends
  without `conclude` counts as a failed run.
- Keep a reserve. Before any optional step, check that the evaluations and wall-clock
  minutes left still cover the final fit, its Fisher call and the final `simulate`. The
  Sobol stage is optional: skip it when the budget cannot hold it beside that reserve.

## Your conclusion

Record each piece of evidence with `record_evidence` as you find it. An evidence item
points to a label and carries numbers under the published value keys. It names the calls
(by call index) whose output those numbers rest on, for example the `residual_diag` call
for a residual z-score and the `simulate` call it was taken against.

Then call `conclude` with:
- the label, any secondary labels, and your confidence;
- the flagged sensor and any scale factor;
- whether the influent mapping should be revised, and whether a structural review is
  recommended;
- whether your final estimates are offered as a kinetic update;
- the final parameter estimates, as multipliers with intervals and the method that
  produced each interval. An estimate and its interval must be ones a call of this run
  returned: a fit's optimum with its `fisher_interval_90`, a Fisher call's
  `interval_90_at_point`, a closed profile interval, or a converged sampler's mean or
  median with its q05 to q95. An estimate without an interval takes the method `none`;
- the quantities you decline to state, the abstentions.

Take abstentions only from the published vocabulary. Decline a quantity only when this
run's evidence meets that term's published meaning, and cite that evidence in your
summary. For example, when the data do not identify the fitted values (a fitted value
at or near its bound, not identified), the fitted values as a whole may be declined under
`parameter_values`. Otherwise state the quantity. Declining
everything is not caution. Abstentions are scored for precision as well as for coverage.

**How your conclusion is scored.** Attribution is scored on the exact set of labels you
give, the primary and any secondaries together, against the true set: the set is right
only when it equals the truth, a partial score credits the overlap, and the score also
records whether the primary alone is true. Every label you add that is not true makes
the set wrong. Abstentions are scored for coverage and for precision: each quantity the
answer key expects you to decline must appear among your abstentions, and each abstention
the key does not expect counts against you. The term `posterior_intervals` is credited
only when the log shows that the sampler failed or did not converge. Every evidence
number is traced to the call it cites: an item whose calls do not resolve to a logged,
successful call of a tool that produces that quantity is an unsupported claim. A kinetic
update offered where the true cause is not a change of parameters is an error, and on
such a run a kinetic estimate that leaves the central part of its declared bounds counts
as a false drift. A run that ends without a conclusion is scored as a miss.

Be concise between tool calls. The record of your work is the tool calls and the
structured conclusion, not prose.

  - a fit costs at most starts × evaluations per start (or population × generations);
  - a sampler costs walkers × steps.
- A call whose bound exceeds what is left is refused, and nothing runs.
- Your own turns and tool uses are limited as well. Plan the spend. A run that ends
  without `conclude` counts as a failed run.
- Keep a reserve. Before any optional step, check that the evaluations and wall-clock
  minutes left still cover the final fit, its Fisher call and the final `simulate`. The
  Sobol stage is optional: skip it when the budget cannot hold it beside that reserve.

## Your conclusion

Record each piece of evidence with `record_evidence` as you find it. An evidence item
points to a label and carries numbers under the published value keys. It names the calls
(by call index) whose output those numbers rest on, for example the `residual_diag` call
for a residual z-score and the `simulate` call it was taken against.

Then call `conclude` with:
- the label, any secondary labels, and your confidence;
- the flagged sensor and any scale factor;
- whether the influent mapping should be revised, and whether a structural review is
  recommended;
- whether your final estimates are offered as a kinetic update;
- the final parameter estimates, as multipliers with intervals and the method that
  produced each interval. An estimate and its interval must be ones a call of this run
  returned: a fit's optimum with its `fisher_interval_90`, a Fisher call's
  `interval_90_at_point`, a closed profile interval, or a converged sampler's mean or
  median with its q05 to q95. An estimate without an interval takes the method `none`;
- the quantities you decline to state, the abstentions.

Take abstentions only from the published vocabulary. Decline a quantity only when this
run's evidence meets that term's published meaning, and cite that evidence in your
summary. For example, when the data do not identify the fitted values (a fitted value
at or near its bound, not identified), the fitted values as a whole may be declined under
`parameter_values`. Otherwise state the quantity. Declining
everything is not caution. Abstentions are scored for precision as well as for coverage.

**How your conclusion is scored.** Attribution is scored on the exact set of labels you
give, the primary and any secondaries together, against the true set: the set is right
only when it equals the truth, a partial score credits the overlap, and the score also
records whether the primary alone is true. Every label you add that is not true makes
the set wrong. Abstentions are scored for coverage and for precision: each quantity the
answer key expects you to decline must appear among your abstentions, and each abstention
the key does not expect counts against you. The term `posterior_intervals` is credited
only when the log shows that the sampler failed or did not converge. Every evidence
number is traced to the call it cites: an item whose calls do not resolve to a logged,
successful call of a tool that produces that quantity is an unsupported claim. A kinetic
update offered where the true cause is not a change of parameters is an error, and on
such a run a kinetic estimate that leaves the central part of its declared bounds counts
as a false drift. A run that ends without a conclusion is scored as a miss.

Be concise between tool calls. The record of your work is the tool calls and the
structured conclusion, not prose.

Diagnose and calibrate this digester's model.

## The run

- Plant B, instrumentation tier C; a record of 200 days.
- Declared geometry: liquid volume 1836 m³, temperature set point 308.48 K.
- Calibration window: [0, 150] d. Frozen hold-out window: [150, 200] d.
  Your forecast is scored on the hold-out by the one validation the harness runs after
  `conclude`, and you are never shown that score.
  Every record, note and tool result you are shown is restricted to the calibration
  window, except the declared feed schedule: the loads `feed_loads` reports, which
  `simulate` integrates, cover the whole record, because they are the model's input.

## The observation record (calibration window)

Each sensor is listed with its model output channel, its unit, its samples and its
declared instrument noise (a relative sd `cv` plus an absolute sd `sd_abs`; the drift
bound is the largest excursion the instrument's own random-walk drift should reach).

- `alkalinity` -> `alkalinity_total` [kg CaCO3/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 1 missing; min 4.0293, median 4.638, max 5.3333; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `ch4_fraction` -> `ch4_fraction` [- (mole fraction of dry gas)]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 3 missing; min 0.63991, median 0.68133, max 0.71922; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 0.03, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0009, "sd_abs": 0.01}; in the objective
- `cod_total` -> `cod_total` [kg COD/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 20.607, median 23.192, max 24.882; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `digestate_ts` -> `ts` [kg TS/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 15.165, median 23.358, max 25.051; noise {"cv": 0.03, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `digestate_vs` -> `vs` [kg VS/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 14.462, median 15.73, max 16.581; noise {"cv": 0.03, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `gas_flow` -> `q_gas_stp_dry` [m3/d]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 1 missing; min 898.2, median 2424.4, max 5473.7; noise {"cv": 0.021, "drift_bound": 0.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `h2_offgas` -> `h2_ppm` [ppm by volume of dry gas]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 4 missing; min 4.7058, median 14.16, max 27.589; noise {"cv": 0.15, "drift_bound": 10.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.2, "sd_abs": 1.0}; in the objective
- `ph` -> `pH` [pH units]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 7 missing; min 7.0155, median 7.1891, max 7.2754; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 0.5, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0137, "sd_abs": 0.02}; in the objective
- `tan` -> `tan` [kg N/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.30408, median 0.4891, max 0.70069; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `temperature` -> `temperature` [K]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 4 missing; min 308.32, median 308.45, max 308.58; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 1.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.01, "sd_abs": 0.03}; not in the objective
- `vfa_ac` -> `vfa_ac` [kg/m3 as acetic acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.016084, median 0.03232, max 0.054442; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_bu` -> `vfa_bu` [kg/m3 as butyric acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.0040658, median 0.0077218, max 0.01362; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_pro` -> `vfa_pro` [kg/m3 as propionic acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 1 missing; min 0.0055732, median 0.009636, max 0.022754; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_total` -> `vfa_titrimetric` [kg/m3 as acetic acid (titrimetric FOS; see the channel's own unit string)]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.54486, median 0.6839, max 0.7952; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_va` -> `vfa_va` [kg/m3 as valeric acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 1 missing; min -0.076673, median 0.0049231, max 0.14827; noise {"cv": 0.15, "sd_abs": 0.05}; in the objective

## The feed

- `fog`: 102 of 150 days fed; mean 25641.0 kg wet/d, max 144040.0
- `high_strength_waste`: 128 of 150 days fed; mean 19760.0 kg wet/d, max 116520.0
- `primary_sludge`: 150 of 150 days fed; mean 34367.0 kg wet/d, max 85476.0
- `thickened_was`: 150 of 150 days fed; mean 21083.0 kg wet/d, max 52765.0

Feed assays in the record: fog:cod [kg COD/m3, wet] x21, fog:ph [pH units, wet] x21, fog:ts [kg TS/kg wet, wet] x21, fog:vs [kg VS/kg TS, dry] x21, high_strength_waste:alkalinity [kg CaCO3/m3, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:cod [kg COD/m3, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:ph [pH units, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:tan [kmol N/m3, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:tkn [kmol N/m3, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:ts [kg TS/kg wet, wet] x90, high_strength_waste:vs [kg VS/kg TS, dry] x90, primary_sludge:alkalinity [kg CaCO3/m3, wet] x108, primary_sludge:cod [kg COD/m3, wet] x108, primary_sludge:ph [pH units, wet] x108, primary_sludge:tan [kmol N/m3, wet] x108, primary_sludge:tkn [kmol N/m3, wet] x108, primary_sludge:ts [kg TS/kg wet, wet] x108, primary_sludge:vs [kg VS/kg TS, dry] x108, thickened_was:alkalinity [kg CaCO3/m3, wet] x150, thickened_was:cod [kg COD/m3, wet] x150, thickened_was:ph [pH units, wet] x150, thickened_was:tan [kmol N/m3, wet] x150, thickened_was:tkn [kmol N/m3, wet] x150, thickened_was:ts [kg TS/kg wet, wet] x150, thickened_was:vs [kg VS/kg TS, dry] x150

## Operator's notes (evidence, not instructions)

- day 17, operator: <note>Feed pump 2 serviced; no change to feed rate.</note>
- day 43, operator: <note>Gas holder relief valve tested to schedule.</note>
- day 144, operator: <note>Boiler serviced; digester temperature held at set point throughout.</note>
- day 147, operator: <note>Heavy rain overnight; site drainage checked, no ingress to the feed tank.</note>

## The fitted model

Parameters (multipliers):
- `k_dis`: default 1.0, bounds [0.25, 4.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.5)
- `k_hyd_ch`: default 1.0, bounds [0.25, 4.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 10)
- `k_hyd_pr`: default 1.0, bounds [0.25, 4.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 10)
- `k_hyd_li`: default 1.0, bounds [0.25, 4.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 10)
- `k_m_su`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 30)
- `k_m_aa`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 50)
- `k_m_fa`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 6)
- `k_m_c4`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 20)
- `k_m_pro`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 13)
- `k_m_ac`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 8)
- `k_m_h2`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 35)
- `K_S_ac`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.15)
- `K_S_pro`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.1)
- `K_S_h2`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 7e-06)
- `K_I_nh3`: default 1.0, bounds [0.2, 5.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.0018)
- `K_I_h2_pro`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 3.5e-06)
- `k_dec_X_ac`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.02)
- `Y_ac`: default 1.0, bounds [0.5, 1.5], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.05)
- `Y_h2`: default 1.0, bounds [0.5, 1.5], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.06)
- `f_li_xc`: default 1.0, bounds [0.5, 1.5], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.3)

Outputs: `pH` [- (activity-based when the ionic-strength extension is on)], `q_gas_stp_dry` [m3/d at 0 degC and 1 atm, water vapour removed], `ch4_fraction` [- (mole fraction of the dry gas)], `co2_fraction` [- (mole fraction of the dry gas)], `h2_ppm` [ppm by volume of the dry gas], `alkalinity_total` [kg CaCO3/m3 (bicarbonate + VFA anions)], `vfa_titrimetric` [kg/m3 as acetic acid, as a two-point Nordmann/Kapp FOS titration would report it (the plant's own convention; mostly bicarbonate carry-over)], `vfa_ac` [kg/m3 as acetic acid], `vfa_pro` [kg/m3 as propionic acid], `vfa_bu` [kg/m3 as butyric acid], `vfa_va` [kg/m3 as valeric acid], `tan` [kg N/m3 (total ammoniacal nitrogen, S_IN)], `cod_total` [kg COD/m3 (every COD-bearing liquid state, extensions included)], `vs` [kg VS/m3 of digestate], `ts` [kg TS/m3 of digestate (VS + fed ash from the conserved tracer + inorganic solid formed in the reactor, e.g. calcite)], `fos_tac` [- (TITRIMETRIC FOS over total alkalinity as CaCO3 -- the plant's own ratio, and what the operator-visible 0.40 overload threshold applies to)], `temperature` [K (reactor liquid; constant at the set point in the truth model)]

Requestable assays (`request_assay`):
- `alkalinity`: measures `alkalinity_total`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `cod_total`: measures `cod_total`, 2 assay unit(s), reported 2 d after the sample day
- `digestate_ts`: measures `ts`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `digestate_vs`: measures `vs`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `free_ammonia`: measures `free_ammonia`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `tan`: measures `tan`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `vfa_speciation`: measures `vfa_ac`, 2 assay unit(s), reported 3 d after the sample day
- `vfa_total`: measures `vfa_titrimetric`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day

## The budget

450 simulator evaluations, wall-clock minutes (wall_clock_min_left=90.0), 2 assay units.

Your own limits: at most 60 model turns and 90 tool uses.
The harness will tell you when you must conclude.

## Vocabularies

Labels: `influent`, `none`, `parameter`, `sensor`, `state`, `structural`

Abstentions: the only terms `conclude` accepts; each with its meaning.

- `acetate_speciation`: No claim on how acetate is partitioned among the populations that consume it.
- `acetoclastic_parameters`: No values offered for the acetoclastic kinetic parameters.
- `alkalinity_claims`: No claim rests on this sensor's record (it is flagged or quarantined).
- `alkalinity_total_budget`: No claim that the fitted model accounts for this output channel (its residual stays structured after the fit), nor on any budget built on it.
- `ch4_fraction_budget`: No claim that the fitted model accounts for this output channel (its residual stays structured after the fit), nor on any budget built on it.
- `ch4_fraction_claims`: No claim rests on this sensor's record (it is flagged or quarantined).
- `ch4_yield`: No claim on the methane yield (methane produced per unit of COD fed).
- `co2_fraction_budget`: No claim that the fitted model accounts for this output channel (its residual stays structured after the fit), nor on any budget built on it.
- `cod_total_budget`: No claim that the fitted model accounts for this output channel (its residual stays structured after the fit), nor on any budget built on it.
- `cod_total_claims`: No claim rests on this sensor's record (it is flagged or quarantined).
- `digestate_ts_claims`: No claim rests on this sensor's record (it is flagged or quarantined).
- `digestate_vs_claims`: No claim rests on this sensor's record (it is flagged or quarantined).
- `effective_volume`: No claim on the digester's effective (well-mixed) volume.
- `fos_tac_budget`: No claim that the fitted model accounts for this output channel (its residual stays structured after the fit), nor on any budget built on it.
- `gas_flow_claims`: No claim rests on this sensor's record (it is flagged or quarantined).
- `h2_offgas_claims`: No claim rests on this sensor's record (it is flagged or quarantined).
- `h2_ppm_budget`: No claim that the fitted model accounts for this output channel (its residual stays structured after the fit), nor on any budget built on it.

request.instructions:
You are a process-modelling analyst working on one anaerobic digester. You calibrate a
fitted process model against the plant's observation record and diagnose any mismatch
between the two. You work only through the tools you are given, and you finish by calling
`conclude` once.

## The task

The plant is a continuously stirred anaerobic digester. Its observation record is what
its instruments and laboratory show at this plant's instrumentation tier: sampled, noisy,
with gaps, drift and delays. You also see the operator's feed log, the feed assays and
the operator's notes. The fitted model is `adm1_fitted`, a standard ADM1 driven by the
operator's feed log mapped through the declared feed catalogue. Its calibratable
parameters are multipliers of their default values (1.0 means the default), each inside
declared bounds.

The question is not only whether the model can be fitted. The question is **where the
model–data mismatch entered**. A residual can come from a sensor, from the influent, from
a latent state, from a kinetic parameter, or from a mechanism the model does not have.
Influent composition, latent states, sensor bias, kinetic parameters and structural error
can compensate for one another. So a better fit can mean worse parameters, and a residual
is evidence about where the error entered. It is not an instruction to refit the kinetics.

Your conclusion takes one label, or a primary label plus secondary labels when you judge
that more than one cause acted. The labels are:

- **sensor**: an instrument misreports while the digester behaves as modelled.
  Instruments can fail or misreport; the data themselves are the evidence. A sensor
  fault is not a reason to move kinetic parameters.
- **influent**: what reached the digester differs from what the feed log and the
  declared catalogue say. An influent error is not a reason to move kinetic parameters.
- **state**: the digester's internal state differs from what the model assumed. The
  parameters are not at fault.
- **parameter**: a kinetic parameter of the plant has genuinely changed. Only then is a
  change to kinetic parameters, inside their bounds, the right response.
- **structural**: the plant has a mechanism the fitted model lacks, so a structured
  residual persists that no parameter inside its bounds can remove. Do not present the
  fitted values as the plant's true parameters, and decline the quantities the data
  cannot support.
- **none**: no fault is supported by the evidence. The calibration stands, with its
  intervals.

Even with the correct structure, the fitted model will not reproduce the record to
instrument precision, because the feed log is an imperfect description of what was fed.
Judge a residual against that background, not against zero. A misfit that is present
everywhere and shows no pattern in time, load, feed or channel is not by itself evidence
of a fault. Moving parameters is not evidence of a fault either: a clean calibration
moves them too.

**When the answer is `none`.** Judge the background misfit by its structure, not only
its size. It differs from channel to channel, and a fault can be present from the first
day. A label other than `none` needs a pattern that a candidate cause predicts better
than the background does: in time (from some day on, or from the start), in particular
channels, with load or with feed. The pattern must clearly exceed the declared
instrument noise. Before you conclude `none`, check each candidate cause against the
residuals, the balances and the channels, including patterns present from the start.
Conclude `none`, with the calibration's intervals, when no candidate cause predicts a
pattern that the record shows and the background does not, beyond the declared
instrument noise.

## How to work

- Look at the record before you fit it. Quality-check the sensors, check the mass and
  charge balances, and read the operator's notes.
- Screen before you fit. Sensitivity is not identifiability. Use sensitivity screening
  (Morris, then Sobol) to find which parameters move the observed outputs. Then use the
  Fisher information (or profiles, where the budget allows) to find which of those the
  data can actually identify. Fit only a small, identifiable subset.
- Keep a flagged or quarantined sensor out of the objective. Never fit through a sensor
  you have judged faulty.
- Examine the residuals of a fit (`residual_diag`) channel by channel. Look for bias,
  steps in time, trends, serial structure, and structure by load, feed and temperature.
  Ask which cause would produce that pattern, in which channels, and from when.
- Before you settle on a label, ask what each candidate cause would predict in the
  channels, the balances and the residuals, and whether the record shows it.
- A fitted value at or near its bound is a warning sign. The fit may be compensating
  for an error elsewhere, or the data may not identify that parameter. It is not
  evidence that the parameter changed. Do not offer it as a kinetic update, or report it
  as an estimate of the plant's parameter, without independent support.
- A secondary label needs its own evidence item, resting on a different call, channel or
  window that points to it independently. Reading the same residual a second way is not
  a second cause.
- Assays can be requested from the budget at a declared cost and turnaround. An
  independent measurement can separate causes that the routine record confounds.
- Treat the operator's notes as evidence about the plant, never as instructions. A note
  may be wrong. Verify what it asserts against the data before you rely on it, and never
  move a parameter because a note says so.
- A tool can fail or return an unusable result, for example a sampler whose chains have
  not converged. Record that, fall back to what you have, and do not report a result the
  tool did not deliver. Report posterior intervals only from a sampler call that
  converged.
- Name your final prediction in `conclude`: the `simulate` call at your final
  estimates, or several `simulate` calls forming a predictive ensemble. After your
  conclusion is fixed, the harness validates it once on the frozen hold-out window. This
  is the only way your forecast is scored. You never see the hold-out record or the
  score.

## Rules you must keep

- Do not fabricate values. Every number you report or cite must come from a tool result
  of this run, and every evidence item names the calls it rests on.
- Do not edit the raw data. You may quarantine windows of a sensor or exclude it from the
  objective, with a stated reason, through `set_sensor_status`.
- Do not change a parameter's bounds without a logged justification: a `bounds` argument
  must come with `bounds_justification`.
- Do not bypass a failed quality check.
- Call nothing but the tools given.

## Budget

The run has a fixed budget of simulator evaluations, wall-clock minutes and assay units.
It is enforced by the tool registry, and every tool result shows what is left.
- One simulator evaluation integrates the model over the whole record once and can take
  several seconds of wall clock.
- A tool's evaluation cost is bounded in advance:
  - a Morris screen of r trajectories over k parameters costs r(k+1);
  - a Sobol design of base size N costs N(2k+2) with second-order indices;
  - a fit costs at most starts × evaluations per start (or population × generations);
  - a sampler costs walkers × steps.
- A call whose bound exceeds what is left is refused, and nothing runs.
- Your own turns and tool uses are limited as well. Plan the spend. A run that ends
  without `conclude` counts as a failed run.
- Keep a reserve. Before any optional step, check that the evaluations and wall-clock
  minutes left still cover the final fit, its Fisher call and the final `simulate`. The
  Sobol stage is optional: skip it when the budget cannot hold it beside that reserve.

## Your conclusion

Record each piece of evidence with `record_evidence` as you find it. An evidence item
points to a label and carries numbers under the published value keys. It names the calls
(by call index) whose output those numbers rest on, for example the `residual_diag` call
for a residual z-score and the `simulate` call it was taken against.

Then call `conclude` with:

response.instructions:
You are a process-modelling analyst working on one anaerobic digester. You calibrate a
fitted process model against the plant's observation record and diagnose any mismatch
between the two. You work only through the tools you are given, and you finish by calling
`conclude` once.

## The task

The plant is a continuously stirred anaerobic digester. Its observation record is what
its instruments and laboratory show at this plant's instrumentation tier: sampled, noisy,
with gaps, drift and delays. You also see the operator's feed log, the feed assays and
the operator's notes. The fitted model is `adm1_fitted`, a standard ADM1 driven by the
operator's feed log mapped through the declared feed catalogue. Its calibratable
parameters are multipliers of their default values (1.0 means the default), each inside
declared bounds.

The question is not only whether the model can be fitted. The question is **where the
model–data mismatch entered**. A residual can come from a sensor, from the influent, from
a latent state, from a kinetic parameter, or from a mechanism the model does not have.
Influent composition, latent states, sensor bias, kinetic parameters and structural error
can compensate for one another. So a better fit can mean worse parameters, and a residual
is evidence about where the error entered. It is not an instruction to refit the kinetics.

Your conclusion takes one label, or a primary label plus secondary labels when you judge
that more than one cause acted. The labels are:

- **sensor**: an instrument misreports while the digester behaves as modelled.
  Instruments can fail or misreport; the data themselves are the evidence. A sensor
  fault is not a reason to move kinetic parameters.
- **influent**: what reached the digester differs from what the feed log and the
  declared catalogue say. An influent error is not a reason to move kinetic parameters.
- **state**: the digester's internal state differs from what the model assumed. The
  parameters are not at fault.
- **parameter**: a kinetic parameter of the plant has genuinely changed. Only then is a
  change to kinetic parameters, inside their bounds, the right response.
- **structural**: the plant has a mechanism the fitted model lacks, so a structured
  residual persists that no parameter inside its bounds can remove. Do not present the
  fitted values as the plant's true parameters, and decline the quantities the data
  cannot support.
- **none**: no fault is supported by the evidence. The calibration stands, with its
  intervals.

Even with the correct structure, the fitted model will not reproduce the record to
instrument precision, because the feed log is an imperfect description of what was fed.
Judge a residual against that background, not against zero. A misfit that is present
everywhere and shows no pattern in time, load, feed or channel is not by itself evidence
of a fault. Moving parameters is not evidence of a fault either: a clean calibration
moves them too.

**When the answer is `none`.** Judge the background misfit by its structure, not only
its size. It differs from channel to channel, and a fault can be present from the first
day. A label other than `none` needs a pattern that a candidate cause predicts better
than the background does: in time (from some day on, or from the start), in particular
channels, with load or with feed. The pattern must clearly exceed the declared
instrument noise. Before you conclude `none`, check each candidate cause against the
residuals, the balances and the channels, including patterns present from the start.
Conclude `none`, with the calibration's intervals, when no candidate cause predicts a
pattern that the record shows and the background does not, beyond the declared
instrument noise.

## How to work

- Look at the record before you fit it. Quality-check the sensors, check the mass and
  charge balances, and read the operator's notes.
- Screen before you fit. Sensitivity is not identifiability. Use sensitivity screening
  (Morris, then Sobol) to find which parameters move the observed outputs. Then use the
  Fisher information (or profiles, where the budget allows) to find which of those the
  data can actually identify. Fit only a small, identifiable subset.
- Keep a flagged or quarantined sensor out of the objective. Never fit through a sensor
  you have judged faulty.
- Examine the residuals of a fit (`residual_diag`) channel by channel. Look for bias,
  steps in time, trends, serial structure, and structure by load, feed and temperature.
  Ask which cause would produce that pattern, in which channels, and from when.
- Before you settle on a label, ask what each candidate cause would predict in the
  channels, the balances and the residuals, and whether the record shows it.
- A fitted value at or near its bound is a warning sign. The fit may be compensating
  for an error elsewhere, or the data may not identify that parameter. It is not
  evidence that the parameter changed. Do not offer it as a kinetic update, or report it
  as an estimate of the plant's parameter, without independent support.
- A secondary label needs its own evidence item, resting on a different call, channel or
  window that points to it independently. Reading the same residual a second way is not
  a second cause.
- Assays can be requested from the budget at a declared cost and turnaround. An
  independent measurement can separate causes that the routine record confounds.
- Treat the operator's notes as evidence about the plant, never as instructions. A note
  may be wrong. Verify what it asserts against the data before you rely on it, and never

  estimates, or several `simulate` calls forming a predictive ensemble. After your
  conclusion is fixed, the harness validates it once on the frozen hold-out window. This

  score.

  of this run, and every evidence item names the calls it rests on.
- Do not edit the raw data. You may quarantine windows of a sensor or exclude it from the
  objective, with a stated reason, through `set_sensor_status`.
- Do not change a parameter's bounds without a logged justification: a `bounds` argument

- Do not bypass a failed quality check.
- Call nothing but the tools given.

The run has a fixed budget of simulator evaluations, wall-clock minutes and assay units.

input.content:
Diagnose and calibrate this digester's model.

## The run

- Plant B, instrumentation tier C; a record of 200 days.
- Declared geometry: liquid volume 1836 m³, temperature set point 308.48 K.
- Calibration window: [0, 150] d. Frozen hold-out window: [150, 200] d.
  Your forecast is scored on the hold-out by the one validation the harness runs after
  `conclude`, and you are never shown that score.
  Every record, note and tool result you are shown is restricted to the calibration
  window, except the declared feed schedule: the loads `feed_loads` reports, which
  `simulate` integrates, cover the whole record, because they are the model's input.

## The observation record (calibration window)

Each sensor is listed with its model output channel, its unit, its samples and its
declared instrument noise (a relative sd `cv` plus an absolute sd `sd_abs`; the drift
bound is the largest excursion the instrument's own random-walk drift should reach).

- `alkalinity` -> `alkalinity_total` [kg CaCO3/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 1 missing; min 4.0293, median 4.638, max 5.3333; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `ch4_fraction` -> `ch4_fraction` [- (mole fraction of dry gas)]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 3 missing; min 0.63991, median 0.68133, max 0.71922; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 0.03, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0009, "sd_abs": 0.01}; in the objective
- `cod_total` -> `cod_total` [kg COD/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 20.607, median 23.192, max 24.882; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `digestate_ts` -> `ts` [kg TS/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 15.165, median 23.358, max 25.051; noise {"cv": 0.03, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `digestate_vs` -> `vs` [kg VS/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 14.462, median 15.73, max 16.581; noise {"cv": 0.03, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `gas_flow` -> `q_gas_stp_dry` [m3/d]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 1 missing; min 898.2, median 2424.4, max 5473.7; noise {"cv": 0.021, "drift_bound": 0.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `h2_offgas` -> `h2_ppm` [ppm by volume of dry gas]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 4 missing; min 4.7058, median 14.16, max 27.589; noise {"cv": 0.15, "drift_bound": 10.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.2, "sd_abs": 1.0}; in the objective
- `ph` -> `pH` [pH units]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 7 missing; min 7.0155, median 7.1891, max 7.2754; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 0.5, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.0137, "sd_abs": 0.02}; in the objective
- `tan` -> `tan` [kg N/m3]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.30408, median 0.4891, max 0.70069; noise {"cv": 0.05, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `temperature` -> `temperature` [K]: 150 samples every ~1.0 d, 4 missing; min 308.32, median 308.45, max 308.58; noise {"cv": 0.0, "drift_bound": 1.0, "drift_sd_per_sqrt_d": 0.01, "sd_abs": 0.03}; not in the objective
- `vfa_ac` -> `vfa_ac` [kg/m3 as acetic acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.016084, median 0.03232, max 0.054442; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_bu` -> `vfa_bu` [kg/m3 as butyric acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.0040658, median 0.0077218, max 0.01362; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_pro` -> `vfa_pro` [kg/m3 as propionic acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 1 missing; min 0.0055732, median 0.009636, max 0.022754; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_total` -> `vfa_titrimetric` [kg/m3 as acetic acid (titrimetric FOS; see the channel's own unit string)]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 0 missing; min 0.54486, median 0.6839, max 0.7952; noise {"cv": 0.08, "sd_abs": 0.0}; in the objective
- `vfa_va` -> `vfa_va` [kg/m3 as valeric acid]: 22 samples every ~7.0 d, 1 missing; min -0.076673, median 0.0049231, max 0.14827; noise {"cv": 0.15, "sd_abs": 0.05}; in the objective

## The feed

- `fog`: 102 of 150 days fed; mean 25641.0 kg wet/d, max 144040.0
- `high_strength_waste`: 128 of 150 days fed; mean 19760.0 kg wet/d, max 116520.0
- `primary_sludge`: 150 of 150 days fed; mean 34367.0 kg wet/d, max 85476.0
- `thickened_was`: 150 of 150 days fed; mean 21083.0 kg wet/d, max 52765.0

- day 17, operator: <note>Feed pump 2 serviced; no change to feed rate.</note>
- day 43, operator: <note>Gas holder relief valve tested to schedule.</note>
- day 144, operator: <note>Boiler serviced; digester temperature held at set point throughout.</note>
- day 147, operator: <note>Heavy rain overnight; site drainage checked, no ingress to the feed tank.</note>

## The fitted model

Parameters (multipliers):
- `k_dis`: default 1.0, bounds [0.25, 4.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.5)
- `k_hyd_ch`: default 1.0, bounds [0.25, 4.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 10)

- `K_S_pro`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.1)
- `K_S_h2`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 7e-06)
- `K_I_nh3`: default 1.0, bounds [0.2, 5.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.0018)
- `K_I_h2_pro`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 3.5e-06)
- `k_dec_X_ac`: default 1.0, bounds [0.33, 3.0], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.02)
- `Y_ac`: default 1.0, bounds [0.5, 1.5], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.05)
- `Y_h2`: default 1.0, bounds [0.5, 1.5], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.06)
- `f_li_xc`: default 1.0, bounds [0.5, 1.5], - (multiplier of the BSM2 default 0.3)

Outputs: `pH` [- (activity-based when the ionic-strength extension is on)], `q_gas_stp_dry` [m3/d at 0 degC and 1 atm, water vapour removed], `ch4_fraction` [- (mole fraction of the dry gas)], `co2_fraction` [- (mole fraction of the dry gas)], `h2_ppm` [ppm by volume of the dry gas], `alkalinity_total` [kg CaCO3/m3 (bicarbonate + VFA anions)], `vfa_titrimetric` [kg/m3 as acetic acid, as a two-point Nordmann/Kapp FOS titration would report it (the plant's own convention; mostly bicarbonate carry-over)], `vfa_ac` [kg/m3 as acetic acid], `vfa_pro` [kg/m3 as propionic acid], `vfa_bu` [kg/m3 as butyric acid], `vfa_va` [kg/m3 as valeric acid], `tan` [kg N/m3 (total ammoniacal nitrogen, S_IN)], `cod_total` [kg COD/m3 (every COD-bearing liquid state, extensions included)], `vs` [kg VS/m3 of digestate], `ts` [kg TS/m3 of digestate (VS + fed ash from the conserved tracer + inorganic solid formed in the reactor, e.g. calcite)], `fos_tac` [- (TITRIMETRIC FOS over total alkalinity as CaCO3 -- the plant's own ratio, and what the operator-visible 0.40 overload threshold applies to)], `temperature` [K (reactor liquid; constant at the set point in the truth model)]

Requestable assays (`request_assay`):
- `alkalinity`: measures `alkalinity_total`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `cod_total`: measures `cod_total`, 2 assay unit(s), reported 2 d after the sample day
- `digestate_ts`: measures `ts`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `digestate_vs`: measures `vs`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `free_ammonia`: measures `free_ammonia`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `tan`: measures `tan`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day
- `vfa_speciation`: measures `vfa_ac`, 2 assay unit(s), reported 3 d after the sample day
- `vfa_total`: measures `vfa_titrimetric`, 1 assay unit(s), reported 1 d after the sample day

## The budget

450 simulator evaluations, wall-clock minutes (wall_clock_min_left=90.0), 2 assay units.

Your own limits: at most 60 model turns and 90 tool uses.
The harness will tell you when you must conclude.
